Article 16
(1) The City Government in efforts to Protect women and children is responsible for:
a. establishing and implementing policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children,
b. making efforts to prevent acts of Violence against women and children including criminal acts of trafficking in persons,
c. increasing the effectiveness of services for women and children victims of acts of Violence,

(2) The responsibility of the City Government in efforts to Protect women and children as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by PD in accordance with their duties and functions and may coordinate with relevant agencies.

It also creates institutional mechanisms across PD (regional apparatus) via Pokja and especially “Focal Point” in each PD (Pasal 11) with duties tied to gender-responsive planning/budgeting and data. These are concrete institutionalization measures, and they were present in the retrieved passages ([2.4-4], [2.4-9], [2.4-8]). The judge’s “Yes” is therefore supported by the source text, implying the golden “No” is likely incorrect.

4.4.rationale: The original Indonesian text includes explicit prevention-through-education/awareness measures. Pasal 17 states prevention is done via “menyelenggarakan sosialisasi” on preventing violence by optimizing roles of “lembaga adat, Pendidikan, budaya, agama...” (explicitly naming education). Pasal 64 also mentions “sosialisasi, seminar dan penyuluhan” regarding child protection and rights, and developing “model sekolah ramah Anak.” These are clear education/awareness-based prevention actions. The retrieved candidates included Pasal 17 ([4.4-20]) and Pasal 64 excerpt ([4.4-83]), so the judge’s “Yes” is well-grounded. This suggests the golden label “No” is likely wrong.
